title: Point-to-Point Integration Sprawl
summary: Systems are integrated through many individually built point-to-point interfaces, each with its own mapping, semantics and quality handling.

relationships.title: Each Data Element Has an Authoritative Source

body_markdown:
# Point-to-Point Integration Sprawl

## Problem

Every new need creates another direct interface; the number of interfaces grows towards n × (n−1).

## Symptoms

- Nobody has an overview of interfaces.
- The same data transformed differently in several interfaces.
- Changes in one system break unknown consumers.

## Root Causes

- Project-by-project funding; no integration architecture or authoritative sources.

## Consequences

- High change cost; inconsistent data; fragile landscape.

## Detection

- Interface inventory and [[Data Lineage|lineage]] show multiple copies of the same entity with different transformations.

## Remediation

- Designate authoritative sources; introduce hubs or shared platforms; govern interfaces with [[Data Contract|contracts]].

## Alternative Patterns

[[Master Data Hub]], [[Change Data Capture]] to a shared platform, [[Data Contract]].

## When It May Be Acceptable

Very few systems with stable interfaces.
